study_identification_part.si_4_title: Judged by your neighbors: A novel framework for personalized assessment of brain structural aging effects in diverse populations

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Datasets listed in the paper include NAKO, ADNI, MACS, AIBL, NIFD, and OASIS3. MACS is not available in the provided dataset list, so it is captured as "Unknown".
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Our study includes data from the German National Cohort (NAKO)... the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) ... the M¨unster-Marburg Affective Disorder Cohort (MACS) ... the Australian Imaging, Biomarker Lifestyle Study of Aging (AIBL) ... the Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Neuroimaging Initiative (NIFD), and the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies 3 (OASIS3)."

answer.NAKO: normative model training; downsampled subsets for stability analysis training

answer.ADNI: test data for neurodegeneration detection; healthy control validation for stability analysis

answer.MACS: healthy control validation for stability analysis

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Training uses NAKO for normative model fitting. ADNI, AIBL, OASIS, and NIFD provide additional test data for neurodegeneration evaluation. MACS and ADNI provide healthy control validation subsets for stability analysis.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The training data for fitting models of the different normative modeling approaches comprised 30,047 samples from the population-based NAKO cohort..."; "To investigate each normativity marker's effectiveness... additional data involving 5,857 participants were utilized, sourced from ADNI, AIBL, OASIS and NIFD datasets"; "Validation subsets included n=835 healthy control participants from the MACS study... and an additional n=1073 healthy older adults from the ADNI study"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Leenings2024.pdf.md: 5.2.1 Training and Test Data; Data for Stability Analysis

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Healthy control normative training sample derived from NAKO after age-based exclusions (22-72 years).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The training data for fitting models of the different normative modeling approaches comprised 30,047 samples from the population-based NAKO cohort... We exclude age groups below 22 years and above 72 years due to small sample sizes (n < 100), which restricts the final sample to 29,883."
